overview:
Gil Cisneros, the Democratic incumbent, advanced to the general election against Republican Eric Ching in a district that leans Democratic by about eight points. Cisneros has raised roughly $705,000 and holds about $260,000 on hand, while Ching has raised under $100,000, giving the incumbent a decisive financial advantage. Prediction markets put Cisneros's chances near 96%.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the incumbent's money edge, and market pricing. All of these point the same direction: a comfortable Democratic win, with the main uncertainty being how large the final margin turns out to be.
